title: Sports ground booking scope
idea: Scoping a sports ground booking system means fixing the slot rules, the actors and their use cases, the no-double-booking guarantee, and what v1 leaves out.
points: Players search grounds, see a court's hourly grid, hold slots, pay and cancel.
The core rule: one court hour belongs to at most one live booking.
Slots start on the hour; one booking covers one to three hours.
Out of v1: recurring bookings and team payments. Assume busy evenings and weekends.

hero.title: Actors and use cases in v1

edges.caption: A player picks a sport, a city and a date, and gets matching grounds.
Opening a ground shows each court as a row of hourly slots: free, held or booked.
Choosing one to three neighbouring hours creates a hold. Nobody else can take them meanwhile.
Paying before the hold expires confirms the booking at the price shown.
A confirmed booking can be cancelled. The refund depends on how early the player cancels.

edges.label: rain, repairs
edges.caption: The ground admin can close a court. Every booking it hits is cancelled with a full refund.

edges.label: expires
edges.caption: The system is an actor too. It frees holds that were never paid.

code.title: Slot rules as checks
code.caption: The v1 booking rules written as one function, then tried on eight requests. Each rule is a stated assumption you can change.

walk.text: Opening hours, the longest booking, how far ahead you may book, and a fixed today.
Three valid requests: a weekday morning, a weekday evening, a Saturday.
Slots are whole hours. Half-hour starts and long bookings are refused first.
The date must be today or later, and within the booking window.
The whole booking must end by closing time, not only its first hour.
Peak means a weekend, or any hour starting between 17:00 and 21:00.

pitfalls: Agree on slot length and alignment before drawing classes; everything else depends on it.
State opening hours, booking window and scale as assumptions, not facts.
Do not forget the admin and the timer; both change booking state.

quiz.q: A team wants the same court every Tuesday for three months. What do you do in v1?
options: Add a recurring flag to TimeSlot right away
Mark it out of scope; later, create many bookings
Let them hold the slots for three months
Refuse to design anything until it is specified
quiz.why: Recurring bookings are a later feature. If v1 handles single bookings well, a series becomes many ordinary bookings created together.

takeaway: Fix slot rules, actors and the no-double-booking rule before any class.

starters: Should slots be fixed hours or free start and end times?
How long should an unpaid hold last for a court?
Which scale assumptions should I state for a booking app like this?
